title: Usage‑adjusted on‑prem credits and maintenance fallback schedule
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Experiment to evaluate a usage-adjusted license credit system for Private/VPC and on‑prem customers, paired with a formalized maintenance fallback schedule. Goal: reduce sales friction for mid‑market customers who demand predictable seatless pricing while preserving enterprise-grade contractual protections and upgrade cadence clarity. The experiment will test (1) a baseline flat annual license fee + usage credits model, (2) a hybrid model where credits scale with committed throughput bands, and (3) a capped-overage model with expedited patch SLAs as a premium add‑on. Each model is paired with documented upgrade windows and an express hotfix SLA option for customers that purchase the premium support tier. Key constraints: align with legal/finance on revenue recognition and with security/compliance on acceptable upgrade push mechanisms for air‑gapped installs.
acceptance_criteria: Define three clear pricing matrices (flat, hybrid-banded, capped-overage) with example TCO for 3 customer archetypes: SMB, Growth SaaS, and Regulated Enterprise.
Legal sign-off on contract language for credits, overage billing, and emergency hotfix clauses.
Security & Compliance confirmation on upgrade channels (KMS/HSM key rotation, audit log retention) for each support tier.
Pilot cohort of 6 existing Private customers agree to test hybrid-banded model for 3 months.
GA launch plan with documentation, sales playbook, and console billing UI ticket created.
success_metrics: Pilot conversion rate >= 40% to paid hybrid option
Reduction in sales cycle time for Private deals by 20% for customers in pilot cohort
No security questionnaire failures attributable to upgrade cadence language during pilot
< 2 support escalations related to billing disputes per 100 customer‑months during pilot
risks: Revenue recognition complexities for banded credits — finance may require minimum commitment thresholds.
Enterprise customers may reject automatic upgrade language for air‑gapped installs; will need manual approval path.
Operational burden: tiered hotfix SLA increases oncall/resourcing requirements for engineering and support.
Security questionnaires may require additional artifacts (attestations, KMS flow diagrams) delaying procurement.
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: finalize pricing matrices and contract templates with Legal & Finance
Week 3-4: onboard pilot customers and instrument billing telemetry for credits usage
Week 5-8: run pilot, collect cost/latency/CSAT data, record any security QA items
Week 9-10: review pilot, iterate pricing, produce sales playbook and support runbooks
Week 11-12: decide GA vs extended pilot and prepare console billing UI tickets for implementation
notes: This ticket focuses on packaging and commercial language; separate ENG tickets should handle implementation of metering, UI, and billing exports. Coordinate with Dedicated team on capacity guarantees tied to committed throughput bands.
